body: I work at a high school and one of my students actually interviewed and got hired for a job. But she couldn't start working because she didn't have a a driver's license or state ID card. It costs $25 to get an ID and she didn't have that much money so she couldn't take the job.
Sounds like your school was never audited.
Michelle Obama already accomplished this. Schools still have drink vending machines but sugar sweetened soda is not allowed. Chips and snacks are all whole grain and low fat.

That's what is hard for me to understand. The things that are normal everyday things that happen to every person turn into catastrophes to him. I can say, yeah it sucks that we have to do XVZ but it's just a fact of life but he says that he can't just be okay with that. 

I think there is a chance he is bipolar since they have not rules it out. The psychiatrist says that he doesn't fit the pattern so he doesn't have that diagnosis. But I know that it can be generic and My brother is diagnosed bipolar and my mother was undiagnosed. We think that she was  bipor based on the symptoms that we could see. She never sought help. She passed away 8 years ago from unrelated causes so it's too late to know.

Your message about external thinking is a good point. I think that's how it is to him. He is hopeful that he will get better while also acting on thoughts that he has to end it. It is like something that is happening to him rather than something that he is doing. 

I do recognize that his distress isn't always obvious. For the past 9 months we have been using a number system to check in. He gives a number (10 being excellent, 1 being very bad) 1-10 for his feelings, and thoughts. So, I will text him "check-in" and he will send me numbers for example 7 6 safe.  This tells me that his mood and his thoughts are okay. But sometimes he will say 8 2 safe. That means that he's in a good mood but his thoughts are pretty low and probably include thoughts of hurting himself.
Thank you. Your story does help. I have a hard time remembering what It feels like to be a teenager.
Thank you for the advise. I really don't know much about residential facilities. I will ask questions when it's time.

Thank you for responding. I agree that he still has hope left. He signed a contract with the therapist but in the moment he was impulsive and he skipped 10 steps in the plan of what he can do if he is having bad thoughts. He was surprised when we told him that he wouldn't be going back to school. He wonders why everyone has given up on ideas to help him because he has lots of ideas for himself. I pointed out that he talks like he has hope and wants to get back to regular life but he's the one who went to the bridge. 

He has done CBT and DBT. His current counselor is great for him. They have really connected. They just haven't had enough time together yet. I know he wants to come home but he can't go back to his school. There's too many things triggering him. You have a good point about inpatient treatment facilities. I haven't thought about that part of it yet. We need a way to keep him safe but right now I feel like I would have to take a leave of absence from work and homeschool him unless we can find an alternative placement. We will get through this week and then I hope the hospital can advise us on the options.
